the official gazette of belgrave harriers Front page: Mark Shippen shoots for 4.20m in the Southern League pole vault at Battersea.
Mark Shippen, fresh from his victory in the senior southern league match the previous week, headed a large and talented field in the youth's pole vault.

He hurdled to a time of 12.7 seconds, reducing the old mark shared by Mark Shippen and John Fernee by three tenths, and also hacked over eight seconds off the 1500 metres record previously held by Reg.
Pride of place however, must go to our Super-youth Mark Shippen, clearing 4 metres yet again to take 3rd in this senior pole-vault competition.
An event as exciting as any was the pole vault where young Mark Shippen came up against ex-international Jeff Fenge of H.W. It was great to see our man come out on top.
Our junior athletes provided two winners in Peter Crosbie - his 6th successive javelin title - and youth Mark Shippen who collected the pole vault with no opposition.
With our sprinters faster than any who have competed in claret and gold before, Mark Shippen now set about making himself highest ever Belgravian by tackling 4.21 metres in the pole vault.
The javelin run-up gave Peter Crosbie a boost as he launched his second longest throw ever and another to take full advantage of the new equipment was Mark Shippen.

With the summer season now approaching it will be interesting to see how Mark Shippen continues his progress in the pole vault. Last year while still a youth he ranked =22nd in the Nation's Senior list and 5th among the Juniors.
His long jump of 5.60 metres took him to 3rd place and also made sure that his name will go down on the Club Record lists as he beat Mark Shippen's three year old record by 18 centimetres.

Our younger members made their presence felt on both field and the track with Matt King picking up 6 points in the heavy events, Mark Shippen beating all other competitors in the pole vault by nearly half a metre, and an inspired Dave Bailey cut his best 400 metres down to 52.8 and then ran 51.6 in the relay.

Once again the full results have not been received but Bedford won with 143, followed by Epsom & Ewell 137, Hercules Wimbledon 93, Belgrave H 78 (but disqualified) and Surrey AC 75. Mark Shippen was 2nd in the pole vault with 3.80 metres and Martin Scott leapt 6.95 metres for 3rd in the long jump.

We did reasonably well on the field with 'A' string wins coming from Pole Vaulter Mark Shippen and javelin thrower Peter Crosbie but our middle distance and hurdling team members found the opposition tough.
Surprise maximum points came from the shot with Cliff Brooks and John Martin while Mark Shippen returned to form with a 4.10m win in the Pole Vault.
